**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Banana (broad, large leaves visible, with pseudostem in background)
- **Affected parts**: Leaves — large, clearly visible
- **Color**: Extensive, widespread yellowing covering most of the leaf area (not just discrete spots)
- **Pattern**: Uniform to diffuse yellowing across the entire leaf blade; dark brown/black streaks visible along and between veins, particularly prominent in the upper leaf
- **Texture/Shape**: Leaves appear wilted/collapsed and drooping; dark elongated streaks/spots scattered across lower leaf on the yellow background

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Anthracnose**: Typically causes dark, sunken discrete lesions — doesn't match this widespread yellowing
- **Bunchy_Top**: Causes narrow, bunched, stunted leaves with dark vein streaks in green tissue — not matching
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: A fruit tip disease — leaves are affected here, not fruit tips
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Oval/elongated brown spots with yellow halos — pattern would be more discrete, not this total yellowing
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Causes streaky yellow lesions and dark brown/black spots, but usually more discrete lesion patterns on otherwise green leaves
- **Panama_Disease** (Fusarium wilt): Causes progressive, widespread yellowing of older/lower leaves starting at margins, leaves collapse and droop, internal vascular streaking/discoloration — **matches very well**: the nearly complete yellowing of the entire leaf surface, the dark vascular streaking visible throughout, and the collapsed/drooping appearance of the leaves

The hallmarks here — entire-leaf yellowing, leaf collapse/droop, and vascular dark streaking on banana leaves — are classic Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt) symptoms.
